blocks.text: # Proofpress X launch

**Status:** canonical draft
**Channel:** X
**Primary asset:** 30–34 second silent-first launch film
**Source of strategic truth:** `docs/internal/PORTABLE_ARTIFACT_STRATEGY.md`
## Launch decision

The X launch should introduce the day-one wedge, not the entire protocol. The
story is cross-session continuity: two agents are maintaining the same knowledge
artifact without access to each other's conversations. Proofpress gives them a
shared, checkable past so the next agent can continue from the right base without
blindly trusting the latest file.

Portable handoff, semantic diff, the carrier format, npm packaging, and the
long-term collective-intelligence vision support this story but do not all need
to appear in the launch post or film.
## Canonical launch post
The following post is 249 Unicode characters before X link shortening:

> Two agents. One strategy. No shared conversation.
>
> They shouldn’t have to start from zero—or blindly trust the latest file.
>
> Proofpress gives every human and agent a shared, checkable past.
>
> Open source: https://github.com/chenmingtang830/proofpress

Attach the launch film directly to this post. Do not add hashtags, launch emojis,
mentions, a request to repost, or a second call to action.
## Reply thread

The thread is optional. Publish it as replies to the canonical post when there is
time to remain present for discussion. Each reply stays within the standard
280-character limit.
### Reply 1 — the missing layer

> The artifact survives. The decisions that made it disappear.
>
> Chats stay inside sessions. Git records lines and commits. A summary can sound right without being reproducible.
>
> The next agent still has to guess what changed, why, and which paths were already rejected.
### Reply 2 — what gets admitted

> With Proofpress, Session A admits v2 with the actual change, the reason, actor roles, and one consequential rejection.
>
> Proofpress computes the artifact diff and checks whether the recorded change claims match what really changed.
### Reply 3 — what the next agent receives

> Session B cannot see Session A’s conversation. It reads the artifact’s shared history instead: current head, semantic changes, attributed why, rejected paths, and verification results.
>
> Then it continues from the right base—or refuses a stale one.
### Reply 4 — the honesty boundary

> Proofpress does not record raw conversations or private chain of thought. It does not pretend that attributed reasons or unsigned identity are cryptographic truth.
>
> It provides deterministic integrity for captured history, and makes gaps explicit.
### Reply 5 — category and install

> Proofpress is an open protocol and reference implementation for versioned knowledge artifacts with verifiable provenance.
>
> Markdown and static HTML today. More harnesses and carriers next.
>
> Install the alpha: npm install --save-dev proofpress@next
## Video length

Use a 30–34 second film. A longer brand film can exist later, but the X launch
asset needs only one complete proof: Session A records an accepted decision;
Session B, without the conversation, inherits a shared past and continues from
the correct head; a stale actor is refused.

The film must be understandable without narration. Music and sound design may
add rhythm, but the copy, product evidence, and causal sequence must survive
muted autoplay.
## Film script
### Beat 1 — disconnected intelligence, 0:00–0:05
On-screen copy:

```text
TWO AGENTS.
ONE STRATEGY.
NO SHARED CONVERSATION.
```

Visual: two independent session windows occupy opposite sides of the frame. A
single `strategy.md @ v1` sits between them. Neither session has a visual channel
to the other.
### Beat 2 — the continuity gap, 0:05–0:09
On-screen copy:

```text
THE ARTIFACT SURVIVES.
THE DECISIONS DISAPPEAR.
```

Visual: the document stays solid while the surrounding decision context—why,
rejected direction, actor, and base—briefly appears and then dissolves. A
restrained Canvas UI particle treatment may be tested here, but the typography
and artifact must remain readable without it.
### Beat 3 — Session A admits v2, 0:09–0:16
Show a real, simplified Proofpress event:

```text
strategy.md  v1 → v2

changed
position Proofpress as the open trust layer

why
cross-session continuity is the day-one wedge

rejected
build a new approval workflow

change claims  ✓ verified
```

The strategic change and rejection come from the actual Proofpress decision
history. The rendered CLI output must be generated from a safe launch fixture,
not fabricated as an unavailable product surface.
### Beat 4 — Session B inherits the past, 0:16–0:24

Session B begins with no Session A transcript. Show it inspecting the artifact
and recovering the current head, change, attributed why, rejected direction,
and verification result.
On-screen copy:

```text
NO CHAT HISTORY.
NOT STARTING FROM ZERO.
```
Then show the consequence, not another feature list:

```text
continue from v2
avoid the rejected approval workflow
```

This is the film's money moment. Session B acts differently because the artifact
has a shared, checkable past.
### Beat 5 — stale work is refused, 0:24–0:28
Show a third actor attempting to continue from `v1`:

```text
base v1
current head v2

STALE BASE — REFUSED
```
On-screen copy:

```text
NO SILENT OVERWRITE.
```
### Beat 6 — category close, 0:28–0:34
On-screen copy:

```text
PROOFPRESS

THE OPEN TRUST LAYER
FOR AGENT-NATIVE KNOWLEDGE WORK

SCALE INTELLIGENCE.
PRESERVE TRUST.
```
Final frame:

```text
OPEN SOURCE
github.com/chenmingtang830/proofpress
```

Do not put the npm command in the closing frame. The repository URL is the one
X-film call to action; installation belongs in the README and final thread
reply.
## Frame plan

| Time | Frame | Evidence job | Motion |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0:00–0:02 | “TWO AGENTS.” | Establish actors | Hard typographic reveal |
| 0:02–0:03.5 | “ONE STRATEGY.” | Establish shared artifact | Central document resolves |
| 0:03.5–0:05 | “NO SHARED CONVERSATION.” | Establish isolation | Sessions separate laterally |
| 0:05–0:09 | Artifact remains; decisions disappear | Show the continuity gap | Optional particle dissolution |
| 0:09–0:12 | `v1 → v2`, change and why | Show admitted event | Tight terminal crop |
| 0:12–0:16 | Rejection and verified claims | Show negative context and checkable account | Rejection locks; check resolves |
| 0:16–0:20 | Session B inspects without transcript | Recover shared state | Lineage reveals from artifact |
| 0:20–0:24 | B continues from v2 and avoids dead branch | Prove behavioral value | Correct path brightens |
| 0:24–0:28 | Stale v1 is refused | Prove concurrency boundary | Attempt stops at current head |
| 0:28–0:32 | Category and vision | Name the product | Editorial close |
| 0:32–0:34 | Repository URL | Conversion | Hold; no competing motion |
## Visual guardrails
- The artifact is always the stable center; agents and sessions rotate around
it.
- Use the seal and lineage as signals of admitted history, not as claims of
cryptographic identity.
- “Verified” modifies computed changes and change claims, never attributed why
or unsigned actors.
- Use one Canvas UI signature effect at most. HyperFrames owns all timing and
rendering.
- No old review UI, approval controls, thousand-line-diff hook, legacy install
command, or “Markdown gets its own Git” positioning.

- Terminal and artifact text must remain readable at ordinary X playback size.
- Do not show private repository names, local paths, real actor identifiers, or
internal strategy text beyond the approved launch fixture.
## Film acceptance test
After one silent viewing, an unfamiliar developer should be able to answer:

1. Why can Session B continue without Session A's conversation?
2. What did Proofpress preserve that the final document alone did not?
3. Which parts are computed or verified, and which are attributed context?
4. What happens when an agent works from a stale base?

If the viewer answers only “it versions Markdown” or “it makes better diffs,”
the film has failed its strategic purpose.
## Video alt text

> A 30-second motion graphic shows two isolated AI-agent sessions working on the same strategy document. Session A records an accepted change, its attributed reason, a rejected direction, and verified change claims. Session B, without seeing Session A’s conversation, reads that shared history and continues from the correct version. A stale version is refused. The film closes on Proofpress as the open trust layer for agent-native knowledge work.
